subject: Benchmarking onboarding: validation schedule & acceptance artifacts
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: samira@novus-retail.com; ethan.royce@novus-retail.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai; dev.patel@redwood.ai; tessa.morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Benchmarking handoff: initial plan and acceptance criteria

Hi Samira / Ethan —

Following our success call last week, handing over the onboarding benchmark to engineering and CS. Attached is a first-draft benchmark plan (redwood_onboard_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx) that lays out the test windows, traffic profiles, and acceptance criteria we discussed. Key items below — please confirm any constraints on the test dataset and access.

Acceptance targets (proposal):
- Sustained throughput: 200 req/s for the "product-search" route (95th percentile of requests distributed across 3 model routes)
- Tail latency: p99 <= 150ms for 1k token context (baseline); target p95 <= 70ms
- Concurrency: support 180 concurrent active sessions without queueing beyond 50ms
- Stability: no error-rate spikes >0.5% over a 30-minute window during ramp and steady-state

Planned runs:
1) Baseline warm-up (15 min) — validate model warm caches
2) Ramp test (30 min) — linear ramp to peak throughput of 250 req/s to observe backpressure
3) Steady-state endurance (60 min) — sustained throughput at agreed target
4) Burst/chaos spikes (10 x short bursts) — verify graceful degradation and fallback rules

What we need from Novus before we run:
- Shared traffic profile CSV (anonymized request size & token distribution) — ideally by EOD Wed
- Test account + API key scoped for staging (endpoint + IP allowlist or VPN details)
- A contact for procurement/infra if we need to provision Dedicated capacity for the run

Owners:
- Redwood: laura_bennett (onsite coordination), monica_patel (benchmark execution), dev_patel (load harness & infra)
- Novus: Samira Khan (PM), Ethan Royce (platform lead)

Next step: can you confirm a 48-hour window between Thu 12/9 and Tue 12/14 when Novus is available for the baseline + ramp? Once you confirm we will schedule the run, provision load-generation hosts, and share the results template.

Attachments: redwood_onboard_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: Benchmarking handoff: initial plan and acceptance criteria

Laura —

Thanks for the plan; this looks comprehensive. We can provide an anonymized traffic profile (CSV) by end of day Wednesday 12/7. For testing windows, Dec 9 (Thu) is tight for infra team, but Dec 13 (Mon) morning works for a baseline run and Dec 14 (Tue) morning for the ramp + endurance. Can we do both on those two days?

A few constraints from our side:
- We must not run any tests that write to production data stores — only read-only staging with mirror data.
- Our staging cluster has an enforced egress IP range; we'll supply allowlist by Wed.
- If Redwood needs Dedicated capacity, please provide a ballpark estimate of cost and lead time so procurement can pre-approve.

Also: we prefer p99 <= 120ms if achievable — Latency is a big differentiator for our user flows. If that requires model variant changes / quantization trade-offs, flag those in the results.

Samira

Subject: Re: Benchmarking handoff: initial plan and acceptance criteria

Samira / Ethan —

Appreciate the quick reply and the tighter p99 target. A few clarifications from the engineering side so the run yields actionable results:

Load harness & measurement notes:
- We will run the load from two geo-located load generators (us-west/us-east) to approximate your traffic mix. You can supply additional regions if you want a closer shape.
- Traffic profile: please include columns for endpoint, avg_tokens, tail_tokens(95/99), and expected QPS per endpoint. Sample file attached (novus_traffic_profile_v2.csv).
- Cache warm-up: we will perform a 15-minute synthetic warm-up to populate prefix/KV caches. Results reported will separate cold vs warm latency windows.
- P95/p99 calculation window: we use sample windows of 1 minute for ramp and 5 minutes for steady-state; we'll include percentile jitter plots in the final artifact.

Special cases we need you to confirm:
- Are there long-sequence user journeys (>= 2k tokens) that we should test specifically? If yes, send 10 representative sessions (anonymized).
- Any IP allowlist/VPN creds can be sent to dev.patel@redwood.ai — we will not store them in plain text after the run.

Provisioning note: if we see >20% degradation under your expected traffic mix with hosted model variants, we will recommend a brief Dedicated proofing window (48–72 hours) to validate throughput with reserved GPUs. Estimate for that is ~ $6k–$9k for the short proof depending on GPU class; procurement should be able to pre-approve a commit if you want the higher confidence run.

Next operational steps once we have your CSV + creds:
- We will schedule the baseline run (laura to own coordination)
- Dev will provision load generators and share access to real-time Grafana links
- Post-run we will share the baseline-results-template.xlsx pre-filled with run metadata and percentile breakdowns

Thanks —
Monica Patel
Engineering Manager, Onboarding | Redwood Inference
